title: Full course E
abstract: The happy medium: from zero to Class E.

chapters.title: First steps
chapters.abstract: In the first chapter we lay the foundation for the knowledge of the future radio amateur. We concentrate on the knowledge needed to make a first contact in training operation under the guidance and supervision of a radio amateur.

chapters.title: Electrical oscillations and radio waves
chapters.abstract: This chapter teaches the physical basics of electrical oscillations and electromagnetic waves as the foundation of radio engineering. It covers the relationship between voltage, frequency, wavelength and spectrum, and how they are represented and described mathematically. Finally, it explains where radio waves fit into the frequency spectrum in practice, frequency assignment and the amateur bands.

chapters.title: Propagation
chapters.abstract: This chapter describes how radio waves propagate under real atmospheric and ionospheric conditions. It covers the various propagation mechanisms such as ground wave, sky wave and refraction, and how they depend on the time of day, the season and solar activity. It also explains typical effects such as fading, skip zones, skip distance, and the MUF and LUF, which are decisive for radio contacts in practice.

sections.title: Long path and short path I

chapters.title: Amateur stations
chapters.abstract: In this chapter we look at the many different kinds of amateur stations and their call signs. We learn what club stations, remote stations, repeaters, beacons and links are, and we look at amateur stations in special locations such as satellites or the Antarctic.

chapters.title: International operating
chapters.abstract: Thanks to the many frequency bands available to us in amateur radio, radio contacts are not limited to the friend next door. The whole world is our neighbour! Radio waves know no borders; they can reach every spot around the world. This chapter deals with radio contacts with other countries and with operating abroad, for example on holiday.

chapters.title: Current, voltage, resistance, power, energy
chapters.abstract: This chapter teaches the basic electrical quantities current, voltage, resistance, power and energy, and shows how they are physically related. It covers handling electrical circuits safely, measuring electrical quantities, Ohm's law, and components and their properties. It also introduces practical concepts such as alternating current, decibels and circuit symbols, which are essential for understanding modern radio and electronic circuits.

sections.title: The right to build your own equipment

chapters.title: Electromagnetic field
chapters.abstract: This chapter introduces the basic concepts of electric and magnetic fields and shows how the two together form an electromagnetic field. It thus lays the physical foundation for understanding radio waves, antennas and electromagnetic propagation.

chapters.title: Components
chapters.abstract: This chapter teaches the basic properties and interplay of important electronic components such as capacitors, inductors, diodes, transistors and integrated circuits. It forms the basis for understanding electronic circuits and how they work in transmitters, receivers and other radio equipment.

chapters.title: Series and parallel connection of components
chapters.abstract: This chapter covers the basic rules for connecting components in series and in parallel. The aim is to understand the behaviour of simple and mixed networks and, for example, to calculate total resistances, voltages and currents systematically.

chapters.title: Power supplies
chapters.abstract: Radios have to be supplied with electrical voltage and current in order to work. In this chapter we learn the basics of supplying voltage and current with power supply units, batteries and rechargeable batteries. The dangers of electric current are also covered.

chapters.title: Basic circuits
chapters.abstract: This chapter introduces the basic circuit blocks of radio engineering that are needed to generate, process and convert radio-frequency signals. They include filters and tuned circuits, oscillators, mixers, frequency multipliers, amplifiers and frequency converters. These modules form the basis of modern transmitter and receiver circuits.

chapters.title: Modulation
chapters.abstract: In this chapter we look at how so-called modulation makes it possible to impress information such as human speech onto a radio wave. In doing so, we get to know the basic types of modulation, AM, FM and SSB.

chapters.title: Receivers
chapters.abstract: This chapter covers the basic structure of radio receivers and their most important modules and functions. Various receiver concepts are presented, and key properties such as selectivity, gain control, noise performance and frequency generation are explained. The aim is to understand how the individual stages of a receiver work together and how they affect reception.

chapters.title: Transmitters
chapters.abstract: This chapter covers the basic structure of a radio transmitter and how its individual modules work together. Topics include output power, power limiting, measuring equipment and loads, and how unwanted emissions arise and are avoided. A further focus is on electromagnetic compatibility and on dealing responsibly with interference when transmitting.

chapters.title: Log and QSL cards
chapters.abstract: Many radio amateurs record every radio contact in a log and send their contact partners so-called QSO cards to confirm contacts that have taken place. Sometimes the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) also orders log-keeping in order to investigate interference.

chapters.title: Digital transmission methods
chapters.abstract: This chapter deals with digital transmission methods. We learn what distinguishes digital from analogue, the basics of telegraphy and radioteletype, which digital methods are used for voice transmission and what is special about them.

chapters.title: Digital signal processing
chapters.abstract: This chapter examines the basics and applications of digital signal processing, which is essential for modern information processing.

chapters.title: Operating procedure
chapters.abstract: The basics of operating procedure were already covered at the beginning of the course; this chapter is about operating procedure in special circumstances. Specifically, we look at the particular procedure when a station is called by very many other stations at the same time, at amateur radio contests, amateur radio direction finding, image transmission and radio operation in emergencies and disasters.

chapters.title: Antennas and transmission lines
chapters.abstract: This chapter deals with everything to do with antennas and antenna cables. Besides the most important types of antenna, we cover topics such as fitting antenna installations in motor vehicles, protecting people from electromagnetic radiation and safety when putting up and operating an antenna installation.

sections.title: Antenna gain in dBi and dBd

chapters.title: Safety distance for the protection of persons
chapters.abstract: This chapter covers the protection of persons from electromagnetic fields in amateur radio. It introduces the terms ERP and EIRP, explains the legal limits and the notification and authorisation requirements, and shows how safety distances, including those for the protection of persons, are calculated and assessed. The aim is radio operation that is safe and complies with the rules, especially for fixed amateur radio installations.

sections.title: Notification of fixed amateur radio installations
Safety distance for the protection of persons II

chapters.title: Safety
chapters.abstract: This chapter covers key safety aspects of amateur radio operation, from questions of building law and liability to electrical safety and lightning protection. It explains measures such as earthing, equipotential bonding and the safe handling of antennas and electrical equipment. The aim is to minimise risks to people, buildings and equipment and to ensure safe radio operation.

sections.title: Protective earthing and equipotential bonding I

chapters.title: Laws and regulations
chapters.abstract: Amateur radio is subject to national laws and other regulations, most of which are based on international agreements. In this chapter we learn all the legal basics that are important for radio amateurs and have not yet been covered in the course so far.

sections.title: Secrecy of telecommunications and prohibition of interception

chapters.title: Abbreviations
chapters.abstract: When you listen to experienced radio amateurs, you immediately notice the many abbreviations that are used quite naturally in a radio contact or in a personal conversation. We have already met a number of abbreviations in the previous chapters. Further important abbreviations are introduced in this chapter.
